advice.maidclinic.allergic_rhinitis: Antihistamines control symptoms; avoid pollen and dust mites. Antibiotics are useless here.
advice.maidclinic.bacterial_pharyngitis: Bacterial pharyngitis needs a full antibiotic course. Do not stop early when symptoms improve - that risks relapse and resistance.
advice.maidclinic.chronic_gastritis: Eat regularly and avoid spicy food, strong tea and coffee; an antacid can help. Black stool, vomiting blood or weight loss needs care.
advice.maidclinic.dehydration: Sip oral rehydration salts. Little urine, sunken eyes or confusion need medical care.
advice.maidclinic.gastroenteritis: Acute gastroenteritis is usually self-limiting and settles in 1-3 days, but fluids are essential: small sips of oral rehydration salts. Most cases need no antibiotics. Seek care for blood in stool, persistent vomiting or no urine.
advice.maidclinic.healthy: Nothing wrong right now. Regular sleep, a balanced diet and fresh air keep illness away.
advice.maidclinic.heat_exhaustion: Move to shade, loosen clothing, drink electrolyte fluids and cool the body. Do not use ice baths or alcohol rubs.
advice.maidclinic.hypertension: Hypertension needs long-term salt reduction, regular routine and medication; never stop suddenly. Severe headache, chest pain or blurred vision needs urgent care.
advice.maidclinic.hypoglycemia: Give about 15-20 g of fast sugar, recheck after 15 minutes. Never force-feed someone who is unconscious.
advice.maidclinic.insomnia: Fix sleep habits first. Melatonin is only a short-term aid, not a long-term solution.
advice.maidclinic.iron_deficiency_anemia: Iron plus vitamin C, continued for months in real life. Iron-rich food such as red meat and liver also helps.
advice.maidclinic.medication_overuse: Stop the antipyretic and observe; drink water. Persistent vomiting, jaundice or worsening pain needs care.
advice.maidclinic.minor_burn: Cool with running water for 20 minutes, then cover with a clean dressing. No ice, toothpaste, soy sauce or grease, and do not burst blisters.
advice.maidclinic.osteoporosis: Osteoporosis needs calcium plus vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise and sunlight. Sudden severe back pain or inability to stand may mean a fracture.
advice.maidclinic.type_2_diabetes: Type 2 diabetes needs less refined sugar, regular meals and long-term medication. Do not use glucose tablets unless hypoglycaemia is confirmed.
advice.maidclinic.viral_uri: Most colds are viral and settle in 5-7 days. Rest and fluids; use an antipyretic only above 38.5 C or when uncomfortable. Antibiotics do not help.
advice.maidclinic.wound_infection: Rinse and bandage the wound. Spreading redness, pus or fever means antibiotics and medical review.
book.maidclinic.page.1:
HOME CARE MANUAL
- Maid Clinic

Right-click a maid with the stethoscope:
- Examine first, then treat
- Treat the cause, avoid antibiotics
- Seek help when things worsen

General first aid only; not medical advice.
book.maidclinic.page.10:
9. Long-term care

Hypertension: less salt, regular routine, take medication, never stop suddenly.
Type 2 diabetes: less refined sugar, regular meals, monitor glucose.
Chronic gastritis: regular meals, less spicy food, strong tea and coffee.
Osteoporosis: calcium + vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, sunlight.

Chronic mode is off by default; enable it with /maidclinic chronic on.
book.maidclinic.page.11:
10. Body attributes

Fixed: blood type, height, penicillin allergy, family history, constitution.
Changeable: weight, exercise, salt, sugar, sleep, stress.

The first consultation creates a record. Weight and lifestyle drift slowly depending on care.
Penicillin allergy: use azithromycin instead of amoxicillin.
book.maidclinic.page.12:
11. Illness and work

Illness slows movement and attack damage:
- mild -10%
- moderate -20%
- severe -35%

Severe untreated illness can leave named sequelae: rheumatic heart disease, hypertensive organ damage, diabetic neuropathy, kidney injury, heat-stroke sequelae, chronic wound, cognitive impairment, liver injury. Total cap -15%.

Disable with /maidclinic efficiency off; existing sequelae are suspended while disabled.
book.maidclinic.page.13:
12. Doctor badges

Equip a badge in a maid bauble slot; she will treat other maids within 8 blocks.

- Intern: mild, 55%, 30 s
- Resident: moderate, 70%, 20 s
- Attending: severe, 85%, 12 s
- Chief: severe, 95%, 8 s

Successful treatments grant XP (1 + severity); 4/10/20 XP promotes her. The badge tier is the cap.
A sick doctor has 15% lower success.
book.maidclinic.page.2:
1. Fever

Axillary temperature 37.3 C or higher.
- Below 38.5 C: fluids, rest, cooling
- 38.5 C or uncomfortable: paracetamol 0.5 g, 4-6 h apart, max 2 g/day, no more than 3 days in a row
- No alcohol rubs, no ice baths
- Fever over 3 days, breathlessness or confusion: seek care
book.maidclinic.page.3:
2. Oral rehydration salts

With diarrhoea, vomiting or heavy sweating, fluids matter more than stopping the diarrhoea.

WHO reduced-osmolarity ORS (ORS III) per litre: sodium chloride 2.6 g, potassium chloride 1.5 g, trisodium citrate 2.9 g, glucose 13.5 g.

Mix the whole sachet as instructed; do not split it or mix with juice or milk. Sip often; little urine or drowsiness needs care.
book.maidclinic.page.4:
3. Antibiotics

- Work only on bacteria, not on viral colds
- Finish the full course even after feeling better
- Never share or self-increase doses
- Misuse harms gut flora and breeds resistance

Colds, flu and most acute diarrhoea need no antibiotics.
book.maidclinic.page.5:
4. Wounds and burns

Wound: rinse with clean water, remove debris, cover with a sterile dressing.

Burn: cool under running water for 20 minutes, then cover.
- No ice
- No toothpaste, soy sauce or grease
- Do not burst blisters
- Large, facial or joint burns need medical care
book.maidclinic.page.6:
5. Heat and low blood sugar

Heat exhaustion: shade, loosen clothing, electrolyte fluids, active cooling. Confusion or very high temperature needs urgent care.

Hypoglycaemia: about 15-20 g of fast sugar when shaky and sweaty, recheck after 15 minutes; never force-feed if unconscious.
book.maidclinic.page.7:
6. Red flags

- Breathlessness, chest pain, altered consciousness
- High fever over 3 days
- Persistent vomiting, blood in stool, no urine for 8 hours
- Rapidly spreading redness or pus
- Seizures, fainting

Stop self-treating and seek help.
book.maidclinic.page.8:
7. Prevention

- Wash hands, ventilate rooms
- Mask up when ill
- Regular sleep, balanced food, exercise
- Regular checkups and a health record
- Sign a family doctor agreement for long-term care

Stay healthy, you and your maid.
book.maidclinic.page.9:
8. References

- WHO, Oral Rehydration Salts (2006)
- NHS, Burns and scalds
- ADA, Low Blood Glucose (Hypoglycemia)
- Chinese guideline on clinical use of antibiotics (2015)
- IDSA GAS pharyngitis guideline (2012)
- Diagnostics, 9th ed.

Game-based education only; not medical advice.
book.maidclinic.page.14:
13. Chronic condition: Hypertension

Blood pressure stays high; early on there may be no symptoms. Headache, dizziness, neck tightness and tinnitus can occur.
Long-term risk: damage to heart, brain and kidneys.
In game: limit salt, control weight, keep a regular routine, take antihypertensives as prescribed and do not stop suddenly; recheck with the sphygmomanometer.
Red flags: severe headache, chest pain, blurred vision, confusion.
book.maidclinic.page.15:
14. Chronic condition: Type 2 diabetes

Common signs: excessive thirst, urination and appetite, weight loss, fatigue, blurred vision.
Long-term risk: peripheral neuropathy, kidney disease, retinopathy.
In game: limit refined sugar and total calories, eat regularly, monitor glucose, take antidiabetics long-term as prescribed.
Note: do not use antidiabetics during hypoglycaemia; seek help for acetone breath, vomiting or confusion.
book.maidclinic.page.16:
15. Chronic condition: Chronic gastritis

Common signs: epigastric pain, post-meal fullness, acid reflux, belching, nausea.
Long-term risk: recurring symptoms, malnutrition and, rarely, bleeding.
In game: eat regularly; reduce spicy food, strong tea, coffee and alcohol; take antacids as prescribed.
Red flags: black stool, vomiting blood, marked weight loss, difficulty swallowing.
book.maidclinic.page.17:
16. Chronic condition: Osteoporosis

Common signs: back pain, reduced height, fracture after minor trauma.
Long-term risk: fractures and reduced mobility.
In game: calcium + vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, moderate sunlight, long-term supplementation as prescribed.
Red flags: sudden severe back pain or inability to stand may mean a fracture; seek help.

Chronic conditions are disabled by default; enable with /maidclinic chronic on.
